The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix. If $X\sim N_d(m,\Sigma)$, then its law has Lebesgue density
$$f_{m,\Sigma}(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2} \exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-m)^T\Sigma^{-1}(x-m)\right), \qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

Assume AC and use the directional convention of
[[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. For probability measures $P,Q$ on one
measurable space, $D(P\|Q)\ge0$, and $D(P\|Q)=0$ if and only if $P=Q$.

There is also the following normalized-density identity. Let
$(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space: it is a set
with a sigma-algebra and measure ([[def-measure-space]]), and there is a
countable measurable cover by sets of finite $\mu$-measure
([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). Let
$\gamma:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable function with
$Z:=\int\gamma\,d\mu\in(0,\infty)$, and put $\pi=\gamma/Z$. Let
$q:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable probability density,
so $\int q\,d\mu=1$, and suppose $q=0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on
$\{\gamma=0\}$. Assume
$$\int q\bigl(|\log\gamma|+|\log q|\bigr)\,d\mu<\infty,$$
where each term with $q=0$ is defined to be zero. Then
$$\log Z =\int q(\log\gamma-\log q)\,d\mu +D(q\,\mu\|\pi\,\mu).$$
In particular, the first integral is at most $\log Z$. This identity concerns
normalized densities only; it does not assert posterior existence for an
unspecified statistical model.

derivations.claim: Let $g$ be the everywhere-positive Gaussian density in [F1] with mean $m$ and covariance $K$. Since $f$ is a Lebesgue density and $g>0$ everywhere, the law $P_f$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $P_g$. The log ratio is integrable: $\int f\ln f$ is finite by hypothesis, while $\ln g$ is a constant plus a quadratic form and $X$ has finite second moments. Hence $$D(P_f\|P_g)=\int f\ln(f/g)=-h(X)+\frac d2\ln(2\pi)+\frac12\ln\det K+\frac12\mathbb E[(X-m)^TK^{-1}(X-m)].$$ The last expectation is $\operatorname{tr}(K^{-1}K)=d$, by expanding the finite quadratic form and using the covariance entries.

By [F2], the left side in step 1.1 is nonnegative, which rearranges to the displayed entropy bound. Equality holds exactly when $D(P_f\|P_g)=0$, which by [F2] is equivalent to equality of the laws; thus $X\sim N_d(m,K)$. Conversely, substituting the density $g$ into the entropy integral gives equality because its centered quadratic expectation is $d$.

citations.quote: If $X$ has Lebesgue density $f$ on $\mathbb R^d$ and $\int f\ln f$ is a finite real number, its differential entropy in nats is $h(X):=-\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)\ln f(x)\,dx$. If $(X,S)$ has conditional densities $f_{X|S=s}$ for almost every $s$ and the indicated integral is finite, set $h(X|S):=\int h(f_{X|S=s})\,dP_S(s)$. We use only these finite-integral cases; differential entropy is not defined here by a formal subtraction of possibly infinite quantities.

derivations.claim: Let $q(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/2}$ and $M=\max\{1,\|f\|_\infty\}$. On $\{f>1\}$, $f\ln f\le f\ln M$, so the positive part is integrable. For $t\ge0$, $t\ln(1/t)\le1/e$; with $t=f/q$, this gives $f\ln(q/f)\le q/e$. Thus on $\{f\le1\}$, $$-f\ln f=f\ln(q/f)-f\ln q\le q/e+f|\ln q|.$$ The right side is integrable because $q$ is a probability density and $|\ln q|$ is bounded by a constant plus $|x|^2/2$. Hence the negative part of $f\ln f$ is integrable.
Both parts of $f\ln f$ are integrable by step 1.1. Therefore $\int f|\ln f|<\infty$, and [F1] defines a finite differential entropy.

Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite nonempty alphabet, let $P$ be a probability vector on $\mathcal A$ in the sense of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]], and let $n\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{supp}(P):=\{a\in\mathcal A:P(a)>0\}$. For $a^n=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal A^n$, its empirical distribution is $\widehat P_{a^n}(a):=n^{-1}|\{t:a_t=a\}|$. For $\delta>0$, define the support-restricted strongly typical set by
$$T_\delta^{(n)}(P):=\{a^n\in\operatorname{supp}(P)^n:|\widehat P_{a^n}(a)-P(a)|\le\delta P(a)\text{ for every }a\text{ with }P(a)>0\}.$$
For a finite joint law $P_{XA}$ and a fixed $x^n$, write $T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{A|X}\mid x^n):=\{a^n:(x^n,a^n)\in T_\delta^{(n)}(P_{XA})\}$. This conditional set is empty if $x^n$ is outside the support of $P_X$. Zero-probability letters are excluded exactly, so no logarithm of zero occurs in likelihood calculations on these sets.

derivations.claim: Fix $a\in\mathcal A$ with $P(a)>0$, and set $B_i=\mathbf1_{\{X_i=a\}}$. The variables $B_i$ are IID Bernoulli with mean $P(a)$ and variance $P(a)(1-P(a))\le1/4$. Thus $\widehat P_{X^n}(a)=n^{-1}\sum_iB_i$ has mean $P(a)$ and variance at most $1/(4n)$. If $Z=\widehat P_{X^n}(a)-P(a)$, then pointwise $\mathbf1_{\{|Z|>\delta P(a)\}}\le Z^2/(\delta^2P(a)^2)$. Taking expectations bounds the deviation probability by $1/(4n\delta^2P(a)^2)$.

If $P(a)=0$, then $\Pr[X_i=a]=0$ for each $i$, so the probability that the word contains $a$ is zero by a finite union bound. There are finitely many positive-mass letters; summing the bounds from step 1.1 over them and adding the zero support event shows that the probability of failure of any condition in [F1] tends to zero.

A **real scalar Gaussian relay network** has finite node set $[N]$, source set $\mathcal S\subseteq[N]$, destination set $\mathcal D\subseteq[N]$, one real input $X_i$ and output $Y_i$ at each node, and channel equations
$$Y_j=\sum_{i=1}^N g_{ji}X_i+Z_j,\qquad j\in[N],$$
where the gains $g_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ are fixed and the noises $Z_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables, independent across channel uses and of all source messages. At each use the current noise vector is independent of all past observations and the current inputs; future inputs may depend on past noises through feedback. Node $i$ has average power constraint $\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[X_{i,t}^2]\le P_i$. Each source has an independent uniform message. A length-$n$ causal code uses measurable encoders $X_{i,t}=f_{i,t}(M_i,Y_i^{t-1})$ and destination decoders based on $(Y_d^n,M_d)$, where $M_d$ is its own source message when $d\in\mathcal S$ and a singleton otherwise; multicast means every destination must decode every other source message, while its own message is already known. The average error probability is the probability that any required destination estimate is wrong. Write $G_{B,A}$ for the matrix with rows indexed by $B$ and columns by $A$ whose entries are $g_{ji}$.

Rates in this page's Gaussian formulas are measured in bits per use, $R_i=n^{-1}\log_2|\mathcal M_i|$.

All logarithms, mutual informations and rates in this lemma are in nats. Consider a memoryless network with finite node set $[N]$, source set $\mathcal S$, destination set $\mathcal D$, and independent uniform source messages, each required by every destination. Alphabets are either all finite, as in [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]], or finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with constant coordinates allowed. Encoders are measurable functions of a node's own message and its past outputs; a destination knows its own message. Choose a finite variable $Q$ and measurable kernels with joint law
$$P_Q\prod_k P_{X_k|Q}\,W(dy_{[N]}|x_{[N]})\prod_k P_{\hat Y_k|X_k,Y_k,Q}.$$
Assume AC in the Euclidean case. For each positive-probability $q$, require a measurable version of the local log likelihood
$$\iota_{k,q}=\log\frac{dP_{\hat Y_k|X_k,Y_k,q}}{dP_{\hat Y_k|X_k,q}}(\hat Y_k)$$
to exist and be square-integrable under the target law. For a destination $d$, nonempty $A\subseteq[N]\setminus\{d\}$, and $U\subseteq A^c\setminus\{d\}$, put $C_0=(A\cup U)^c$, let $P_{d,q}$ be the target marginal law of $(X_{[N]},\hat Y_{[N]},Y_d)$ given $q$, and define
$$Q_{d,A,U,q}=P_{X_{A^c},\hat Y_{C_0},Y_d|q}\prod_{k\in A}P_{X_k|q}\prod_{k\in A\cup U}P_{\hat Y_k|X_k,q}.$$
Require $P_{d,q}\ll Q_{d,A,U,q}$ with a measurable square-integrable log likelihood under $P_{d,q}$. Require all mutual informations in the following cut expression to be finite:
$$F_d(A)=I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c}|X_{A^c},Q)-I(Y_A;\hat Y_A|X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c},Q).$$
These likelihood and finiteness hypotheses hold automatically for finite alphabets; zero-mass target atoms are omitted. At any chosen constrained node let $c_k\ge0$ be a measurable input cost. Require either $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)^2]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)]<\Gamma_k$, or a deterministic input whose cost is at most $\Gamma_k$. The latter case includes an identically zero input under a zero budget. Unconstrained nodes and constant coordinates are permitted.

Every nonnegative rate tuple satisfying
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}r_k<F_d(A)$$
for every $d\in\mathcal D$ and nonempty $A$ with $d\notin A$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ is achievable by deterministic measurable causal codes. Each constrained node can satisfy $\sum_{t=1}^m c_k(X_{k,t})\le m\Gamma_k$ on every realized transmitted input sequence of code length $m$, and hence also its expected average-cost constraint. The closure of the union of these regions over admissible laws is achievable. Constant reconstructions are permitted. The separate all-zero tuple is achievable whenever one can choose fixed inputs obeying any imposed costs, regardless of negative cut expressions.

Assume AC. Let $U,V,Y,S$ take values in standard-Borel spaces. Then
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(U;Y|S)+I(V;Y|U,S)$$
and also
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(V;Y|S)+I(U;Y|V,S),$$
where these are equalities of extended nonnegative quantities. In particular, if the conditional law of $Y$ given $(U,V,S)$ depends only on $(V,S)$, then
$$I(U;Y|S)\le I(V;Y|S).$$

all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Write $a=\mathrm{SNR}_1$, $b=\mathrm{SNR}_2$, $c=\mathrm{INR}_1$, $d=\mathrm{INR}_2$. Give $M_2$ to receiver 1 and subtract its deterministic codeword. The scalar Gaussian power bound followed by Jensen and the average input constraint gives $R_1\le\log_2(1+a)$. Reflection gives $R_2\le\log_2(1+b)$. The same argument applies when a direct gain vanishes and then forces the corresponding rate to zero. Throughout the proof independent messages give independent user input vectors, regardless of coordinate dependence inside a vector; the additive Fano remainders disappear on division by $n$ and passage to the coding limit.

Reveal $X_2^n$ to receiver 1. The chain rule and independent inputs give the following exact expansion of the two augmented mutual informations: $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)+I(X_2^n;Y_2^n)=h(Y_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)+h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)$. If $P_1=0$, the input vector is zero and this entropy difference and the claimed logarithmic ratio are both zero. Otherwise, if $a\ge d$, the entropy-difference estimate [F6] applies with $s=|h_{11}|^2$, $t=|h_{12}|^2$, $P=P_1$; phases are removed by unit-modulus rotations. This is precisely the coupling condition $|h_{11}|\ge|h_{12}|$: the lower-SNR observation can be formed by scaling the higher-SNR observation and adding circular Gaussian noise of variance $1-t/s$. The proof of [F6] covers zero gains without division by a cross gain. Its unconditioned-output bound therefore yields $R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+b+d)+\log_2((1+a)/(1+d))=\log_2(1+a)+\log_2(1+b/(1+d))$. Only $a\ge d$ is needed. Reflecting the argument gives the second weak sum bound under $b\ge c$, using the reflected noise coupling.

Define $S_1^n=h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n$ and $S_2^n=h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$ using independent receiver noises. Give $S_1^n$ to receiver 1 and $S_2^n$ to receiver 2. Expanding both augmented informations gives $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n,S_1^n)+I(X_2^n;Y_2^n,S_2^n)=h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)$: the positive $h(S_1^n)$ and $h(S_2^n)$ cancel the interference-plus-noise entropies of the two conditional channels. Applying the two conditional-output estimates in [F6] and $h(Z_i^n)=n\log_2(\pi e)$ proves the third displayed weak sum bound. This calculation is valid in every regime and requires no degradation inequality.

Add two copies of receiver 1's Fano bound and one of receiver 2's. Augment receiver 2 by $S_2^n$ and one receiver 1 copy by $X_2^n$. The resulting information sum equals $h(Y_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-2h(Z_1^n)+h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)$. Indeed the three information terms contribute, respectively, $h(Y_1^n)-h(S_2^n)$, $h(S_2^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n)-h(h_{12}X_1^n+Z_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)$, and $h(h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n)-h(Z_1^n)$. The unconditioned, conditional, and entropy-difference estimates of [F6] give $2R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+a+c)+\log_2(1+d+b/(1+c))+\log_2((1+a)/(1+d))$. The only degradation hypothesis is $a\ge d$, exactly as in step 2.1. Reflection proves the displayed $R_1+2R_2$ bound under $b\ge c$. Thus the stated weak regime supplies every required coupling.

In the mixed regime $c\ge b$ and $a>d$, the individual bounds and first sum bound still follow from steps 1.1 and 2.1. For the MAC sum bound, receiver 1 first decodes $M_1$. On the event of correct decoding it subtracts $h_{11}X_1^n$ and obtains $h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$. If $P_2=0$, step 1.1 gives $R_2=0$ and the required MAC sum bound already follows from the individual bound. Otherwise, if $h_{21}\ne0$, scale by $h_{22}/h_{21}$ and add independent circular Gaussian noise of variance $1-|h_{22}/h_{21}|^2$, which is nonnegative because $c\ge b$ and $P_2>0$. Add the known vector $h_{12}X_1^n$ and apply receiver 2's decoder. Coupling this simulation to the one using the true $M_1$ bounds its joint-message error by the sum of the two original errors; a deterministic MAP decoder has no larger average error. Joint-message Fano and the unconditioned-output estimate [F6] give $R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+a+c)$. If $h_{21}=0$, then $b=c=0$ and step 1.1 forces $R_2=0$, so the same sum bound follows immediately. This establishes the exact mixed sum claim, including degenerate gains.

For the mixed weighted bound add the three Fano information terms $I(X_1^n;Y_1^n,S_1^n)$, $I(X_2^n;Y_2^n)$, and $I(X_2^n;Y_2^n,S_2^n|X_1^n)$. The first expands as $h(S_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)+h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)-h(S_2^n)$, the second as $h(Y_2^n)-h(S_1^n)$, and the third as $h(S_2^n)-h(Z_1^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n,X_1^n)-h(Z_2^n)$. Their sum is $h(Y_1^n|S_1^n)+h(Y_2^n)+h(Y_2^n|S_2^n,X_1^n)-h(Z_1^n)-2h(Z_2^n)$. Apply the three corresponding bounds in [F6] to obtain exactly $R_1+2R_2\le\log_2(1+b+d)+\log_2(1+c+a/(1+d))+\log_2(1+b/(1+c))$. This particular weighted estimate is universal and uses no degradation condition. Reflection gives the other mixed regime. Combining the preceding steps proves every displayed inequality with precisely the hypotheses asserted in the statement.

A **finite discrete memoryless relay channel** is the three-node instance of [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]] with source input $X\in\mathcal X$, relay input $X_r\in\mathcal X_r$, relay observation $Y_r\in\mathcal Y_r$, destination observation $Y\in\mathcal Y$, and transition law $W(y_r,y\mid x,x_r)$. Its one-way message $M$ is uniform on $[M]$ and the destination estimates it from $Y^n$.

In the **relay-only causal model**, $X_i=f_i(M)$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y_r^{i-1})$. In the **full output-feedback model**, both encoders know the past pair $(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$, so $X_i=f_i(M,Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$. In either model the channel outputs at time $i$ are drawn from $W(\cdot,\cdot\mid X_i,X_{r,i})$; no encoder sees a current-time output before choosing its current input. The rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$, and achievability uses average error under the uniform message law.

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$,

$$I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)\ge0.$$

Equality holds if and only if, for every $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional joint pmf factors as $p_{XY|z}=p_{X|z}p_{Y|z}$; this is conditional independence given $Z$.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

Let $Q,X,Z,Y$ be finite random variables and suppose the channel law $P_{Y|X,Z,Q}$ depends on $Q$ only through $(X,Z)$; equivalently, $Q-(X,Z)-Y$ is a Markov chain. Then
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)\ge I(X;Y\mid Z,Q).$$
Thus, for a fixed finite channel and fixed side information $Z$, averaging input laws over a time-sharing variable cannot increase the average conditional mutual information.

derivations.claim: Fano's inequality gives $(1-P_e)\ln|\mathcal M|\le I(M;Y^n)+\ln2$. Apply the chain rule to write $I(M;Y^n)=\sum_i I(M;Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})$.

Since conditional mutual information is nonnegative, each summand is at most $I(M,Y_r^{i-1};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})$. Given $(M,Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$, the current inputs are fixed by causality in either model, and [F1] makes the current output depend on those variables only through $(X_i,X_{r,i})$. Thus the summand equals $I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})$. For the fixed channel $W_Y$, the past $Y^{i-1}$ is a time-sharing variable independent of the current output once the current inputs are fixed. Applying [F5] gives $I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})\le I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i)$.

For the second cut, $I(M;Y^n)\le I(M;Y^n,Y_r^n)=\sum_i I(M;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$. The relay input $X_{r,i}$ is determined by the past. Given the past and $M$, the source input is determined; memorylessness therefore reduces each term to $I(X_i;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1},X_{r,i})$. Conditional on a fixed $X_{r,i}=x_r$, the past is a time-sharing variable for the fixed channel $W_{(Y,Y_r)|X,x_r}$. Applying [F5] and averaging over $X_{r,i}$ bounds the term by $I(X_i;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid X_{r,i})$.

Let $Q$ be uniform on $[n]$ and conditionally draw $(X,X_r,Y_r,Y)$ according to the time-$Q$ joint law induced by the code and channel. Steps 2.1, 2.2 imply both cut inequalities with conditioning on $Q$. Dividing the Fano bound by $n$, then taking a sequence of codes with $P_e\to0$, gives the stated outer bound after closure and convexification.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

All mutual informations and rates in this item are measured in bits; differential entropies in the proof are in nats and are divided by $\ln2$.

In the real Gaussian multicast network of [[def-real-gaussian-multicast-relay-network]], take independent Gaussian inputs $X_i\sim N(0,P_i)$ and independent Gaussian test-channel noises. For a chosen node set $\mathcal Q\subseteq[N]$, set $\hat Y_i=Y_i+\hat Z_i$ with $\hat Z_i\sim N(0,1)$ for $i\in\mathcal Q$ and let $\hat Y_i$ be constant otherwise. Every nonnegative rate tuple satisfying
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k<I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c\cap\mathcal Q}\mid X_{A^c})-I(Y_{A\cap\mathcal Q};\hat Y_{A\cap\mathcal Q}\mid X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c\cap\mathcal Q})$$
for every destination $d\in\mathcal D$ and every cut $A\subseteq[N]$ with $d\notin A$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ is achievable under the stated average-power constraints. The closure of the union of these strict regions over the stated choices, together with the all-zero tuple, is achievable.

In the special case $P_i=P>0$ for every node and $\mathcal Q=[N]$, a noise-level evaluation gives the sufficient cut inequalities
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k < \frac12\log_2\det\!\left(I+\frac P2G(A)G(A)^T\right)-\frac{|A|}{2}$$
for every $A\subseteq[N]$ with $A^c\cap\mathcal D\ne\varnothing$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$, where $G(A)=G_{A^c,A}$. Their closure is achievable. The all-zero rate tuple is always achievable by singleton source-message sets, independently of whether these cut right-hand sides are nonnegative.

A **real scalar Gaussian relay network** has finite node set $[N]$, source set $\mathcal S\subseteq[N]$, destination set $\mathcal D\subseteq[N]$, one real input $X_i$ and output $Y_i$ at each node, and channel equations
$$Y_j=\sum_{i=1}^N g_{ji}X_i+Z_j,\qquad j\in[N],$$
where the gains $g_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ are fixed and the noises $Z_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables, independent across channel uses and of all source messages. At each use the current noise vector is independent of all past observations and the current inputs; future inputs may depend on past noises through feedback. Node $i$ has average power constraint $\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[X_{i,t}^2]\le P_i$. Each source has an independent uniform message. A length-$n$ causal code uses measurable encoders $X_{i,t}=f_{i,t}(M_i,Y_i^{t-1})$ and destination decoders based on $(Y_d^n,M_d)$, where $M_d$ is its own source message when $d\in\mathcal S$ and a singleton otherwise; multicast means every destination must decode every other source message, while its own message is already known. The average error probability is the probability that any required destination estimate is wrong. Write $G_{B,A}$ for the matrix with rows indexed by $B$ and columns by $A$ whose entries are $g_{ji}$.

Rates in this page's Gaussian formulas are measured in bits per use, $R_i=n^{-1}\log_2|\mathcal M_i|$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. If a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^d$ has a Lebesgue density, finite mean $m$, positive-definite covariance $K$, and finite differential entropy $h(X)=-\int f\ln f$, then
$$h(X)\le \frac12\ln\bigl((2\pi e)^d\det K\bigr).$$
Equality holds exactly when $X$ has the Gaussian law $N_d(m,K)$.

Let $M$ be uniform on a finite message set $\mathcal M$ of size $m\ge2$, let $S$ take values in a finite set $\mathcal S$, and let $Y$ take values in $\mathbb R^d$; a complex observation space $\mathbb C^k$ is identified with $\mathbb R^{2k}$. Suppose $Y\mid(M,S)$ has a Lebesgue density. For every measurable estimator $\widehat M=\phi(Y,S)$ with $\phi:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\to\mathcal M$ and error probability $\epsilon$, define $H(M\mid Y,S):=\int H(p_{M|y,s})\,dP_{Y,S}(y,s)$ using its finite posterior vector. Then
$$H(M\mid Y,S)\le h_b(\epsilon)+\epsilon\ln(m-1)\le\ln2+\epsilon\ln m,$$
where $h_b(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ and $0\ln0=0$. For $m=1$, the conditional entropy is zero.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and let $T:V\to V$ be
self-adjoint. Then $V$ has an orthonormal basis consisting of eigenvectors of
$T$.

Assume AC. Let $U,V,Y,S$ take values in standard-Borel spaces. Then
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(U;Y|S)+I(V;Y|U,S)$$
and also
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(V;Y|S)+I(U;Y|V,S),$$
where these are equalities of extended nonnegative quantities. In particular, if the conditional law of $Y$ given $(U,V,S)$ depends only on $(V,S)$, then
$$I(U;Y|S)\le I(V;Y|S).$$

Let $f$ be a Lebesgue probability density on $\mathbb R^d$ with $\|f\|_\infty<\infty$ and $\int |x|^2f(x)\,dx<\infty$. Then $\int f(x)|\ln f(x)|\,dx<\infty$, so the differential entropy in [[def-it-real-differential-entropy]] is a finite real number.

derivations.claim: Fix a destination $d\in A^c$. Give the messages of nodes in $A^c$ to that destination, and also give it all outputs $Y_{A^c}^n$. Since rates are bits and Fano's bound is in nats, [F4] gives $$n\ln2\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k\le I(M_{A\cap\mathcal S};Y_{A^c}^n\mid M_{A^c})+o(n).$$ By the conditional chain rule [F6], expand the mutual information across time. For time $i$, condition on $H_i=(M_{A^c},Y_{A^c}^{i-1})$. Each input in $A^c$ is then fixed by causality in [F2]. The current outputs depend on messages in $A$ only through the current inputs $X_{A,i}$, so conditional data processing [F6] gives $$I(M_{A\cap\mathcal S};Y_{A^c,i}\mid H_i)\le I(X_{A,i};Y_{A^c,i}\mid H_i).$$ The right side is the mutual information of $G(A)X_{A,i}+Z_{A^c,i}$ under the conditional input law given $H_i$.

For almost every $h$, the conditional input second moment given $H_i=h$ is finite, since its average is bounded by the node power constraints. The conditional output is a translate of a Gaussian convolution, so its density is bounded by the standard Gaussian noise peak; [F7] makes its differential entropy finite. Let $K_{i,h}$ be the conditional covariance of $X_{A,i}$ given $H_i=h$. The channel noise is independent with covariance $I$, so [F3] bounds each conditional mutual information in step 1.1, measured in nats, by $$\frac12\ln\det(I_{|A^c|}+G(A)K_{i,h}G(A)^T).$$ Set $\bar K=n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E[K_{i,H_i}]$. Since covariance trace is at most the corresponding second moment and each node's average power is at most $P$, $\bar K\succeq0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\bar K\le |A|P$.

For positive-definite matrices $B,B_0$, let $C=B_0^{-1/2}BB_0^{-1/2}$. Its eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ are positive by [F5], and $\ln\lambda_j\le\lambda_j-1$ because $u-1-\ln u$ has derivative $1-1/u$, decreases on $(0,1]$, increases on $[1,\infty)$, and vanishes at $1$. Thus $$\ln\det B\le\ln\det B_0+\operatorname{tr}(B_0^{-1}(B-B_0)).$$ Apply this with $B=I+G K_{i,h}G^T$ and $B_0=I+G\bar K G^T$, then average over $i,h$; the trace term averages to zero. Hence the average natural log determinant in step 2.1 is at most $\ln\det(I+G\bar K G^T)$. The spectral theorem gives $\bar K\preceq\operatorname{tr}(\bar K)I$, since every nonnegative eigenvalue is at most their sum; hence $G\bar K G^T\preceq |A|P GG^T$. If $0\prec C\preceq D$, then $C^{-1/2}DC^{-1/2}=I+E$ for some $E\succeq0$, so its eigenvalues are at least one and $\det C\le\det D$. Applying this order property and dividing the Fano bound in step 1.1 by $n\ln2$ yields $$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k\le\frac{1}{2\ln2}\ln\det(I_{|A^c|}+|A|P GG^T).$$

Put $a=|A|$ and $b=|A^c|$; both are positive. For any positive-semidefinite $H$ of size $m$, $I_m+aPH\preceq2a(I_m+(P/2)H)$, so determinant monotonicity gives $$\frac{1}{2\ln2}\ln\det(I_m+aPH)\le\frac12\log_2\det(I_m+(P/2)H)+\frac m2\log_2(2a).$$ The block determinant of $\begin{pmatrix}I_b&\sqrt{aP}G\\-\sqrt{aP}G^T&I_a\end{pmatrix}$, computed by taking either identity block as the Schur complement pivot, gives $\det(I_b+aPGG^T)=\det(I_a+aPG^TG)$. Apply the previous inequality once in dimension $b$ and once in dimension $a$, then use this identity to take the smaller additive term. The cut-set outer bound is at most $$\frac12\log_2\det\!\left(I+\frac P2GG^T\right)+\frac12\min(a,b)\log_2(2a).$$

Write $D(A)=\frac12\log_2\det(I+(P/2)G(A)G(A)^T)$, so the sufficient lower bound in [F1] is $L(A)=D(A)-a/2$. Step 4.1 gives the cut-set outer value $O(A)\le D(A)+\frac12\min(a,b)\log_2(2a)=L(A)+\Delta(A)$. If $L(A)>0$, the exact NNC expression satisfies $N_d(A)\ge L(A)$, so $O(A)-N_d(A)\le\Delta(A)$. If $L(A)\le0$, use the separately achievable zero-rate tuple from [F1]; then $O(A)\le L(A)+\Delta(A)\le\Delta(A)$, so the outer cut is within $\Delta(A)$ of that achievable rate. This proves the cutwise comparison without treating the determinant expression as the exact NNC rate and covers negative sufficient-cut values.

The two-user Gaussian interference channel has independent messages, separate encoders, and outputs
$$Y_1=h_{11}X_1+h_{21}X_2+Z_1,\qquad Y_2=h_{12}X_1+h_{22}X_2+Z_2.$$

Rates are bits per use. A scalar Gaussian mutual information is $\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})$, where $\kappa=1/2$ in the real model and $\kappa=1$ in the complex model.

At either receiver of the Gaussian channel in [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]], independent Gaussian codebooks with powers $P_1,P_2$ achieve every nonnegative rate pair for which each nonempty subset $T\subseteq\{1,2\}$ with $\sum_{i\in T}R_i>0$ satisfies
$$\sum_{i\in T}R_i<\kappa\log_2\!\left(1+\sum_{i\in T}|a_i|^2P_i\right),$$
where that receiver observes $Y=a_1X_1+a_2X_2+Z$ with unit-variance real or complex Gaussian noise and $\kappa=1/2$ or $1$, respectively. The codebook symbols are centered $N(0,P_i)$ in the real model and circular $\mathcal{CN}(0,P_i)$ in the complex model. A subset of zero total rate has no false-message candidates and requires no strict inequality; in particular the zero pair is achieved by singleton message sets. The closure of this achievable set is the usual closed Gaussian multiple-access region.

Let $M$ be uniform on a finite message set $\mathcal M$ of size $m\ge2$, let $S$ take values in a finite set $\mathcal S$, and let $Y$ take values in $\mathbb R^d$; a complex observation space $\mathbb C^k$ is identified with $\mathbb R^{2k}$. Suppose $Y\mid(M,S)$ has a Lebesgue density. For every measurable estimator $\widehat M=\phi(Y,S)$ with $\phi:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\to\mathcal M$ and error probability $\epsilon$, define $H(M\mid Y,S):=\int H(p_{M|y,s})\,dP_{Y,S}(y,s)$ using its finite posterior vector. Then
$$H(M\mid Y,S)\le h_b(\epsilon)+\epsilon\ln(m-1)\le\ln2+\epsilon\ln m,$$
where $h_b(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ and $0\ln0=0$. For $m=1$, the conditional entropy is zero.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ take values in standard-Borel spaces. Let their joint law have an arbitrary input marginal $P_{X^n}$ and the memoryless conditional channel law
$$P_{Y^n|X^n}(dy^n|x^n)=\prod_{i=1}^n W_i(dy_i|x_i),$$
where each $W_i$ is a probability kernel. No independence across the input coordinates is assumed. Then, as an inequality in $[0,+\infty]$,
$$I(X^n;Y^n)\le\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_i).$$

Assume AC. Let $U,V,Y,S$ take values in standard-Borel spaces. Then
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(U;Y|S)+I(V;Y|U,S)$$
and also
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(V;Y|S)+I(U;Y|V,S),$$
where these are equalities of extended nonnegative quantities. In particular, if the conditional law of $Y$ given $(U,V,S)$ depends only on $(V,S)$, then
$$I(U;Y|S)\le I(V;Y|S).$$

Assume AC. Let $X$ be real or complex with finite second moment, let $Z$ be independent unit-variance Gaussian noise, and let $Y=aX+Z$. In the real case take $Z\sim N(0,1)$ and $a\in\mathbb R$; in the complex case take $Z\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,1)$ with density $\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$ and $a\in\mathbb C$. Put $v=\mathbb E|X-\mathbb EX|^2$ and $\kappa=1/2$ in the real case, $\kappa=1$ in the complex case. Then
$$I(X;Y)\le\kappa\ln(1+|a|^2v)\le\kappa\ln(1+|a|^2\mathbb E|X|^2)$$
in nats; division by $\ln2$ gives the corresponding bit formula.
Equality in the first inequality holds when $X$ is Gaussian in the real case or circular complex Gaussian in the complex case, including the zero-variance case.

derivations.claim: For the individual bound on $R_1$, give $M_2$ to receiver 1. Fano gives $nR_1\ln2\le I(M_1;Y_1^n|M_2)+o(n)$ in nats. For each fixed $M_2$, $X_2^n$ is fixed; translating $Y_1^n$ by the known vector $-h_{21}X_2^n$ is invertible, so [F5] in both directions preserves this conditional mutual information. The shifted channel from $X_1^n$ is memoryless. The codeword map is deterministic and the channel law depends on $M_1$ only through $X_1^n$, so [F5] in both Markov directions gives $I(M_1;Y_1^n|M_2)=I(X_1^n;h_{11}X_1^n+Z_1^n|M_2)$. Apply [F4] for each $M_2$ and average to bound this by $\sum_iI(X_{1,i};h_{11}X_{1,i}+Z_{1,i})$. By [F6], each term is at most $\kappa\ln(1+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,i})$ nats, where $p_{1,i}=\mathbb E|X_{1,i}|^2$. Jensen's inequality and the power constraint give $R_1\le\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1)$. Exchanging users gives the stated $R_2$ bound.

First suppose both cross gains are nonzero. Receiver 1 first forms its estimate $\widehat M_1$. On the event $\widehat M_1=M_1$, it reconstructs $X_1^n$ and subtracts $h_{11}X_1^n$, obtaining $h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$. Since $|h_{21}|\ge|h_{22}|$, it scales this residual by $h_{22}/h_{21}$ and adds independent Gaussian noise of variance $1-|h_{22}/h_{21}|^2$; for complex channels use circular Gaussian noise. Adding back $h_{12}X_1^n$ gives a simulated $\widetilde Y_2^n$. For the error analysis, construct the same vector using the true $M_1$: it then has exactly the law of receiver 2's $Y_2^n$, and on $\widehat M_1=M_1$ it equals the receiver's simulation. Hence the joint error is at most $P_{e,1}+P_{e,2}$. Since the message pair is finite, the randomized decoder has a deterministic MAP decoder with no larger average error. Exchanging users and using $|h_{12}|\ge|h_{11}|$ gives the symmetric joint decoder at receiver 2.

In the nonzero-cross-gain case of step 1.2, apply the density-observation Fano bound [F3] to the joint decoder at receiver 1. Let $M=(M_1,M_2)$ and $X=(X_1^n,X_2^n)$. The deterministic codeword map and channel law give both Markov directions between $M$ and $X$ with observation $Y_1^n$, so [F5] yields $I(M;Y_1^n)=I(X;Y_1^n)$. The two input vectors are independent because their messages are independent. By [F4], $n(R_1+R_2)\ln2\le I(X_1^n,X_2^n;Y_1^n)+o(n)\le\sum_iI(X_{1,i},X_{2,i};Y_{1,i})+o(n)$. The output variance at time $i$ is at most $1+|h_{11}|^2\mathbb E|X_{1,i}|^2+|h_{21}|^2\mathbb E|X_{2,i}|^2$, because the independent inputs have zero cross covariance after centering. These single-coordinate mutual informations are finite by the power bound and [F6].

For each coordinate put $S_i=h_{11}X_{1,i}+h_{21}X_{2,i}$. The channel output depends on the input pair only through $S_i$, so [F5] in both directions gives $I(X_{1,i},X_{2,i};Y_{1,i})=I(S_i;S_i+Z_{1,i})$. Independence gives $\operatorname{Var}(S_i)\le |h_{11}|^2p_{1,i}+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,i}$; [F6] therefore bounds this term by $\kappa\ln(1+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,i}+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,i})$ nats. Jensen's inequality and the average power constraints yield $R_1+R_2\le\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1+\mathrm{INR}_1)$. The joint decoder at receiver 2 analogously gives $R_1+R_2\le\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_2+\mathrm{INR}_2)$. If $h_{21}=0$, then $h_{22}=0$, so $R_2=0$ by step 1.1; the first sum bound is the $R_1$ individual bound and the second is no tighter because $\mathrm{INR}_2\ge\mathrm{SNR}_1$. If $h_{12}=0$, then $h_{11}=0$, so $R_1=0$ and the second sum bound is the $R_2$ individual bound while the first is no tighter because $\mathrm{INR}_1\ge\mathrm{SNR}_2$. Thus both sum bounds hold also when a cross gain vanishes.

Use the same independent Gaussian codebook ensemble at the two receivers. The finite-receiver construction in the proof of [F2] sums the two ensemble-average errors and jointly selects codebooks meeting both deterministic power constraints, so one codebook pair achieves the intersection of the two Gaussian MAC regions. The strong gain inequalities make each unintended-receiver individual constraint at least as large as the corresponding intended-receiver constraint; the two sum constraints are exactly those displayed. Therefore every rate pair strictly inside the claimed region is achievable, and closure removes strictness.

A **finite discrete memoryless relay channel** is the three-node instance of [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]] with source input $X\in\mathcal X$, relay input $X_r\in\mathcal X_r$, relay observation $Y_r\in\mathcal Y_r$, destination observation $Y\in\mathcal Y$, and transition law $W(y_r,y\mid x,x_r)$. Its one-way message $M$ is uniform on $[M]$ and the destination estimates it from $Y^n$.

In the **relay-only causal model**, $X_i=f_i(M)$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y_r^{i-1})$. In the **full output-feedback model**, both encoders know the past pair $(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$, so $X_i=f_i(M,Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$ and $X_{r,i}=g_i(Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$. In either model the channel outputs at time $i$ are drawn from $W(\cdot,\cdot\mid X_i,X_{r,i})$; no encoder sees a current-time output before choosing its current input. The rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$, and achievability uses average error under the uniform message law.

For either causal model in [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-relay-channel-and-causal-code]], every achievable rate is in the closed convex hull of rate values satisfying, for some finite time-sharing variable $Q$ and law $P_QP_{XX_r|Q}$,
$$R\le I(X,X_r;Y\mid Q),\qquad R\le I(X;Y,Y_r\mid X_r,Q),$$
with the relay transition law used to evaluate the mutual informations. In particular, this is an outer bound; it need not be achievable for relay-only causality.

For a finite relay channel with relay-only causality, fix a finite law $P_{X_r}P_{X\mid X_r}$. Every positive rate
$$0<R<\min\{I(X;Y_r\mid X_r),\ I(X,X_r;Y)\}$$
is achievable, and rate $R=0$ is always achievable with a one-message code. Taking the closure of the union over such laws gives the decode-forward inner bound. Mutual informations use the relay channel law and nats per use.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

Let $Q,X,Z,Y$ be finite random variables and suppose the channel law $P_{Y|X,Z,Q}$ depends on $Q$ only through $(X,Z)$; equivalently, $Q-(X,Z)-Y$ is a Markov chain. Then
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)\ge I(X;Y\mid Z,Q).$$
Thus, for a fixed finite channel and fixed side information $Z$, averaging input laws over a time-sharing variable cannot increase the average conditional mutual information.

derivations.claim: Apply [F2]. Its outer bound has a finite time-sharing variable $Q$ and bounds $I(X,X_r;Y|Q)$ and $I(X;Y,Y_r|X_r,Q)$. Apply [F5] first with input $(X,X_r)$ and no side information, then with input $X$ and side information $X_r$. Averaging over $Q$ cannot increase either conditional mutual information, so both are bounded by the corresponding quantities under the averaged joint input law $P_{X,X_r}$. This gives the displayed maximum as an outer bound.

For achievability, view $(Y_r,Y)$ as the relay's observation and $Y$ as the destination output. This is a finite relay channel whose relay encoder can causally use the observation pair because it has full feedback in [F1]. Apply the block-Markov construction of [F3] with the relay observation $\widetilde Y_r=(Y_r,Y)$; its decoding term becomes $I(X;Y,Y_r|X_r)$, while the destination decoding term is $I(X,X_r;Y)$. Every joint input law factors as $P_{X_r}P_{X|X_r}$, so the construction achieves every rate below the displayed minimum.

The outer bound in step 1.1 and achievable rates in step 1.2 coincide for every joint input law. The joint-input probability simplex is compact. Each mutual information is continuous there because it is a finite sum of terms $-p\ln p$, with $p\ln p$ extended continuously by $0$ at $p=0$; the minimum of the two continuous functions is continuous. It therefore attains a maximum, and taking that maximum and closure proves the capacity formula.

A **finite two-user interference channel** is the two-sender, two-receiver memoryless channel with finite input alphabets $\mathcal X_1,\mathcal X_2$, output alphabets $\mathcal Y_1,\mathcal Y_2$, and transition law $W(y_1,y_2|x_1,x_2)$. Independent uniform messages $M_1,M_2$ are encoded separately as $X_1^n=f_1(M_1)$ and $X_2^n=f_2(M_2)$; receiver $i$ estimates $M_i$ from $Y_i^n$. The **strong-interference regime** means that, for every product law $P_{X_1}P_{X_2}$,
$$I(X_1;Y_1|X_2)\le I(X_1;Y_2|X_2),\qquad I(X_2;Y_2|X_1)\le I(X_2;Y_1|X_1).$$
The inequalities are evaluated under the stated product law and the channel. They are universal hypotheses over input laws, not just inequalities at a chosen optimizing distribution.

Assume the strong-interference inequalities of [[def-finite-two-user-interference-channel-and-strong-regime]]. For independent random vectors $X_1^n,X_2^n$, pass each coordinate through independent uses of the channel. Then
$$I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)\le I(X_1^n;Y_2^n|X_2^n),\qquad I(X_2^n;Y_2^n|X_1^n)\le I(X_2^n;Y_1^n|X_1^n).$$

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

For the average-joint-error no-feedback code of [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac-code]] over the finite DM-MAC, the capacity region is the closure of the union over all finite $Q$ and laws $P_QP_{X_1|Q}P_{X_2|Q}W$ of
$$R_1\le I(X_1;Y\mid X_2,Q),\quad R_2\le I(X_2;Y\mid X_1,Q),\quad R_1+R_2\le I(X_1,X_2;Y\mid Q).$$
Here $Q$ is a public time-sharing variable independent of both private messages; conditional on each $Q=q$, the two input laws are a product. This result does not characterize maximal-error capacity.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

derivations.claim: For any length-$n$ code, independence of the messages makes the induced vectors $X_1^n,X_2^n$ independent. Fano at receiver 1 and the fact that revealing $M_2$ cannot reduce mutual information give $nR_1\le I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)+o(n)$. The analogous receiver-2 bound is $nR_2\le I(X_2^n;Y_2^n|X_1^n)+o(n)$.

Fix finite $Q$ and product conditional input laws. Apply [F4] to the marginal MAC at receiver 1 and to the marginal MAC at receiver 2. Both uses of [F4] generate the same ensemble of independent sender codebooks, because the input laws and time-sharing sequence are the same; only the two decoders differ. Under the strong-interference inequalities [F1], receiver 2's individual bound for sender 1 is at least receiver 1's intended individual bound, and receiver 1's individual bound for sender 2 is at least receiver 2's intended bound. The intersection of the two MAC regions is therefore exactly the three inequalities in the statement.

For the first individual bound, the finite entropy chain rule [F5] and memorylessness give $$I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)=H(Y_1^n|X_2^n)-H(Y_1^n|X_1^n,X_2^n)\le\sum_i I(X_{1,i};Y_{1,i}|X_{2,i}),$$ where the first entropy is at most $\sum_iH(Y_{1,i}|X_{2,i})$ by the chain rule and conditioning, and the second entropy is exactly $\sum_iH(Y_{1,i}|X_{1,i},X_{2,i})$ by the memoryless channel. The same calculation applies to user 2.

By the block-lift inequality [F2], $I(X_2^n;Y_1^n|X_1^n)\ge I(X_2^n;Y_2^n|X_1^n)$. Since $M_2$ is independent of $M_1$, Fano at receiver 2 implies $$H(M_2|Y_1^n,M_1)=H(M_2|M_1)-I(M_2;Y_1^n|M_1)\le H(M_2|M_1)-I(M_2;Y_2^n|M_1)=o(n).$$ Fano at receiver 1 gives $H(M_1|Y_1^n)=o(n)$. Thus $n(R_1+R_2)\le I(M_1,M_2;Y_1^n)+o(n)\le I(X_1^n,X_2^n;Y_1^n)+o(n)\le\sum_i I(X_{1,i},X_{2,i};Y_{1,i})+o(n)$. Exchanging receivers gives the corresponding sum bound at $Y_2$.

Let $Q$ be uniform on $[n]$ and let $(X_1,X_2)$ have the time-$Q$ input law; since the message vectors are independent, $P_{X_1,X_2|Q}=P_{X_1|Q}P_{X_2|Q}$. Combining steps 2.1, 2.2 gives the stated inequalities for this $Q$. Taking limits and closure proves the converse.

The [F4] random-coding proof gives ensemble-average error tending to zero at each receiver under the strict MAC inequalities. The expected sum of the two receiver errors is at most the sum of those two vanishing bounds, so a deterministic codebook pair exists for which both errors tend to zero. Closure removes strictness and the finite variable $Q$ supplies time sharing.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For the real or complex Gaussian interference channel of [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]], assume the strong regime
$$|h_{12}|\ge|h_{11}|,\qquad |h_{21}|\ge|h_{22}|.$$
Then the capacity region is the set of nonnegative rate pairs satisfying
$$R_1\le\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1),\quad R_2\le\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_2),$$
$$R_1+R_2\le\kappa\min\{\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1+\mathrm{INR}_1),\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_2+\mathrm{INR}_2)\},$$
where $\kappa=1/2$ for real and $1$ for complex channels.

The two-user Gaussian interference channel has independent messages, separate encoders, and outputs
$$Y_1=h_{11}X_1+h_{21}X_2+Z_1,\qquad Y_2=h_{12}X_1+h_{22}X_2+Z_2.$$
For the **real model**, $X_i,h_{ji},Z_j$ are real, $Z_j\sim N(0,1)$, and $\mathbb E X_i^2\le P_i$. For the **complex model**, the inputs and gains are complex, $Z_j\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,1)$ with density $\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$, and $\mathbb E|X_i|^2\le P_i$. No feedback is present. For either model define
$$\mathrm{SNR}_1=|h_{11}|^2P_1,\quad \mathrm{SNR}_2=|h_{22}|^2P_2,\quad \mathrm{INR}_1=|h_{21}|^2P_2,\quad \mathrm{INR}_2=|h_{12}|^2P_1.$$
Rates are bits per use. A scalar Gaussian mutual information is $\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})$, where $\kappa=1/2$ in the real model and $\kappa=1$ in the complex model.

For either Gaussian model in [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]], choose private powers $0\le P_{1p},P_{2p}\le P_1,P_2$ and common powers $P_{ic}=P_i-P_{ip}$. Split each message into independent common and private parts, and transmit $X_i=U_i+V_i$ with independent centered Gaussian codewords of powers $P_{ic}$ and $P_{ip}$ (circular in the complex model). At receiver 1, decode $(U_1,V_1,U_2)$ and treat $V_2$ as Gaussian noise of variance $N_1=1+|h_{21}|^2P_{2p}$. At receiver 2, decode $(U_1,U_2,V_2)$ and treat $V_1$ as noise of variance $N_2=1+|h_{12}|^2P_{1p}$. A nonnegative rate split $R_i=R_{ic}+R_{ip}$ is achievable if, at each receiver $j$, every nonempty subset $T$ of its three decoded streams with positive total rate satisfies
$$\sum_{s\in T}R_s<\kappa\log_2\!\left(1+\frac{\sum_{s\in T}|a_{j,s}|^2P_s}{N_j}\right),$$
where $a_{1,1c}=a_{1,1p}=h_{11}$, $a_{1,2c}=h_{21}$, $a_{2,1c}=h_{12}$, and $a_{2,2c}=a_{2,2p}=h_{22}$; $\kappa=1/2$ for real and $1$ for complex channels. A zero-rate stream has a singleton message set and creates no false-message class; the all-zero split is always achievable. The closure of the union over feasible rate splits is an inner region.

For the complex Gaussian channel in [[def-real-two-user-gaussian-interference-channel]], the following are outer bounds in the listed regimes; all logarithms are base two. Write SNR and INR as defined there.

**Weak regime:** If $\mathrm{INR}_1<\mathrm{SNR}_2$ and $\mathrm{INR}_2<\mathrm{SNR}_1$, every achievable pair satisfies
$$R_1\le\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1),\quad R_2\le\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_2),$$
$$R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1)+\log_2\!\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{SNR}_2}{1+\mathrm{INR}_2}\right),$$
$$R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_2)+\log_2\!\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{SNR}_1}{1+\mathrm{INR}_1}\right),$$
$$R_1+R_2\le\log_2\!\left(1+\mathrm{INR}_1+\frac{\mathrm{SNR}_1}{1+\mathrm{INR}_2}\right)+\log_2\!\left(1+\mathrm{INR}_2+\frac{\mathrm{SNR}_2}{1+\mathrm{INR}_1}\right),$$
$$2R_1+R_2\le\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR}_1+\mathrm{INR}_1)+\log_2\!\left(1+\mathrm{INR}_2+\frac{\mathrm{SNR}_2}{1+\mathrm{INR}_1}\right)+\log_2\!\left(\frac{1+\mathrm{SNR}_1}{1+\mathrm{INR}_2}\right),$$

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that

A **real scalar Gaussian relay network** has finite node set $[N]$, source set $\mathcal S\subseteq[N]$, destination set $\mathcal D\subseteq[N]$, one real input $X_i$ and output $Y_i$ at each node, and channel equations
$$Y_j=\sum_{i=1}^N g_{ji}X_i+Z_j,\qquad j\in[N],$$
where the gains $g_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ are fixed and the noises $Z_j$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables, independent across channel uses and of all source messages. At each use the current noise vector is independent of all past observations and the current inputs; future inputs may depend on past noises through feedback. Node $i$ has average power constraint $\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[X_{i,t}^2]\le P_i$. Each source has an independent uniform message. A length-$n$ causal code uses measurable encoders $X_{i,t}=f_{i,t}(M_i,Y_i^{t-1})$ and destination decoders based on $(Y_d^n,M_d)$, where $M_d$ is its own source message when $d\in\mathcal S$ and a singleton otherwise; multicast means every destination must decode every other source message, while its own message is already known. The average error probability is the probability that any required destination estimate is wrong. Write $G_{B,A}$ for the matrix with rows indexed by $B$ and columns by $A$ whose entries are $g_{ji}$.

Rates in this page's Gaussian formulas are measured in bits per use, $R_i=n^{-1}\log_2|\mathcal M_i|$.

All mutual informations and rates in this item are measured in bits; differential entropies in the proof are in nats and are divided by $\ln2$.

$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k<I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c\cap\mathcal Q}\mid X_{A^c})-I(Y_{A\cap\mathcal Q};\hat Y_{A\cap\mathcal Q}\mid X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c\cap\mathcal Q})$$
for every destination $d\in\mathcal D$ and every cut $A\subseteq[N]$ with $d\notin A$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ is achievable under the stated average-power constraints. $$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k < \frac12\log_2\det\!\left(I+\frac P2G(A)G(A)^T\right)-\frac{|A|}{2}$$

> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that

Equality in the first inequality holds when $X$ is Gaussian in the real case or circular complex Gaussian in the complex case, including the zero-variance case.

derivations.claim: If $(T,S)$ are Gaussian-smoothed finite-second-moment variables, then $h(T|S)=h(T-kS|S)\le h(T-kS)\le\log_2(\pi e\operatorname{Var}(T-kS))$ for every complex $k$. The first identity is conditional translation and the first inequality is conditional mutual-information nonnegativity; the second is [F2]. A finite-dimensional convolution with a nonsingular Gaussian has a density bounded by the peak of that Gaussian and finite second moment; [F3], applied after identifying complex vectors with real vectors, therefore makes every relevant joint, marginal, and residual differential entropy finite. In particular the pairs $(Y_1^n,S_1^n)$ and $(Y_2^n,S_2^n)$ have nonsingular independent receiver-noise coordinates, and the degraded pair below has nonsingular joint Gaussian noise when $s>t$. Their conditional entropies are differences of these finite joint and marginal entropies. For conditioning additionally on $X_1^n$, which need not have a density, first subtract its known translated contribution; independence removes that conditioning and leaves the nonsingular smoothed pair $(h_{22}X_2^n+Z_2^n,S_2^n)$. The information-density identity, obtained by integrating the Gaussian conditional density divided by the output density as in [F5], then justifies the remaining conditional entropy identities without infinite subtractions. At zero signal power the same Gaussian density argument applies without alteration. Coordinate entropy chain rules give $h(T^n|S^n)\le\sum_j h(T_j|S_j)$.

Suppose $s>t$ and set $U^n=\sqrt{s}X^n+Z^n$, $V^n=\sqrt{t/s}\,U^n+\sqrt{1-t/s}\,W^n$. The marginal law of $V^n$ is the lower-SNR channel and $X^n-U^n-V^n$ is Markov. Thus the difference of the two output entropies equals $I(X^n;U^n|V^n)=h(U^n|V^n)-n\log_2(\pi e[1-t/s])$: the conditional noise is $Z^n$ given $\sqrt{t/s}Z^n+\sqrt{1-t/s}W^n$. For a coordinate variance $p_j$, minimizing the quadratic residual variance of $U_j$ given $V_j$ gives $(1-t/s)(1+sp_j)/(1+tp_j)$. Step 1.1 therefore bounds the entropy difference by $\sum_j\log_2((1+sp_j)/(1+tp_j))$. This logarithmic ratio has derivative $(s-t)/((1+sp)(1+tp)\ln2)$, which is nonnegative and decreasing. Jensen and the average variance bound yield the first claimed inequality. If $s=t$ the two marginal entropies agree; if $t=0<s$ the same construction and computation apply. If $s=t=0$ both outputs are pure Gaussian noise.

Let $p_{i,j}=\operatorname{Var}(X_{i,j})$. The optimal scalar linear estimate of $Y_{1,j}$ from $S_{1,j}$ has residual variance $1+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j}+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,j}/(1+|h_{12}|^2p_{1,j})$: independence of the two user vectors and the noises eliminates all other covariances. Step 1.1 bounds the conditional entropy by the logarithm of this variance times $\pi e$. The map $x\mapsto x/(1+kx)$ is increasing and concave on $[0,\infty)$ for $k\ge0$, with second derivative $-2k/(1+kx)^3$; hence the residual variance is increasing and concave in the two powers, and its logarithm is also concave and increasing. Jensen and $n^{-1}\sum_jp_{i,j}\le P_i$ give the first conditional-output bound. Reflection gives the second. This calculation has no division by a channel gain and remains valid when any gain vanishes.

The output variances are $1+|h_{11}|^2p_{1,j}+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j}$ and $1+|h_{12}|^2p_{1,j}+|h_{22}|^2p_{2,j}$. Applying the coordinate chain rule, [F2], and logarithmic Jensen gives the two unconditioned-output bounds. Given $X_1^n$, subtract its contribution from $Y_2^n$; independence leaves the linear-estimation problem for $h_{22}X_2^n+Z_2^n$ from $h_{21}X_2^n+Z_1^n$. Its coordinate residual variance is $1+|h_{22}|^2p_{2,j}/(1+|h_{21}|^2p_{2,j})$. The same concavity calculation proves the final conditional bound. Reflection proves its counterpart.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The two-user Gaussian interference channel has independent messages, separate encoders, and outputs
$$Y_1=h_{11}X_1+h_{21}X_2+Z_1,\qquad Y_2=h_{12}X_1+h_{22}X_2+Z_2.$$
For the **real model**, $X_i,h_{ji},Z_j$ are real, $Z_j\sim N(0,1)$, and $\mathbb E X_i^2\le P_i$. For the **complex model**, the inputs and gains are complex, $Z_j\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,1)$ with density $\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$, and $\mathbb E|X_i|^2\le P_i$. No feedback is present. For either model define
$$\mathrm{SNR}_1=|h_{11}|^2P_1,\quad \mathrm{SNR}_2=|h_{22}|^2P_2,\quad \mathrm{INR}_1=|h_{21}|^2P_2,\quad \mathrm{INR}_2=|h_{12}|^2P_1.$$
Rates are bits per use. A scalar Gaussian mutual information is $\kappa\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})$, where $\kappa=1/2$ in the real model and $\kappa=1$ in the complex model.

Let $(X_k)_{k\ge1}$ be IID square-integrable real random variables, with $\mu=\mathbb EX_1$ and $\sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}(X_1)$. For $S_n=\sum_{k=1}^nX_k$,
$$\mathbb E|S_n/n-\mu|^2=\sigma^2/n,$$
and $S_n/n\to\mu$ in $L^2$ and in probability. Also $\mathbb P(|S_n/n-\mu|\ge\varepsilon)\le\sigma^2/(n\varepsilon^2)$ for $\varepsilon>0$.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be real or complex with finite second moment, let $Z$ be independent unit-variance Gaussian noise, and let $Y=aX+Z$. In the real case take $Z\sim N(0,1)$ and $a\in\mathbb R$; in the complex case take $Z\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,1)$ with density $\pi^{-1}e^{-|z|^2}$ and $a\in\mathbb C$. Put $v=\mathbb E|X-\mathbb EX|^2$ and $\kappa=1/2$ in the real case, $\kappa=1$ in the complex case. Then
$$I(X;Y)\le\kappa\ln(1+|a|^2v)\le\kappa\ln(1+|a|^2\mathbb E|X|^2)$$
in nats; division by $\ln2$ gives the corresponding bit formula.
Equality in the first inequality holds when $X$ is Gaussian in the real case or circular complex Gaussian in the complex case, including the zero-variance case.

Assume AC. Let $U,V,Y,S$ take values in standard-Borel spaces. Then
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(U;Y|S)+I(V;Y|U,S)$$
and also
$$I((U,V);Y|S)=I(V;Y|S)+I(U;Y|V,S),$$
where these are equalities of extended nonnegative quantities. In particular, if the conditional law of $Y$ given $(U,V,S)$ depends only on $(V,S)$, then
$$I(U;Y|S)\le I(V;Y|S).$$

derivations.claim: For private rates $p_i\ge0$ and common rates $u_i\ge0$ with $p_i+u_i=r_i$, generate independent Gaussian common codewords $U_i(m_{ic})$ of power $P_{ic}$ and, for every common index, an independent Gaussian satellite codebook $V_i(m_{ic},m_{ip})$ of power $P_{ip}$. Transmit $U_i+V_i$. Receiver 1 uniquely decodes $(m_{1c},m_{1p})$ if some index $m_{2c}$ passes its conditional Gaussian information-density tests; it does not output $m_{2c}$. Its four false-own-message classes have rate exponents $p_1$, $r_1$, $p_1+u_2$, and $r_1+u_2$: respectively wrong private only, wrong own common and its satellite, wrong private and unintended common, and wrong own common and unintended common. Conditional on the correctly indexed layers, a false class has the product law against which its likelihood ratio has mean one. Markov's inequality at a threshold strictly between its rate exponent and its Gaussian mutual information, followed by the union bound, makes its error probability vanish if $p_1<A_1$, $r_1<D_1$, $p_1+u_2<E_1$, $r_1+u_2<G_1$. A wrong unintended index alone is not an error because it leaves the decoded own message unchanged. The true information densities are IID quadratic Gaussian functions with finite variance, so [F2] proves correct-message acceptance; [F3] gives exactly the four displayed Gaussian quantities. Receiver 2 gives $p_2<A_2$, $r_2<D_2$, $p_2+u_1<E_2$, $r_2+u_1<G_2$. Zero-rate or zero-power layers have singleton message sets and no false-message class.

Deterministic power selection is included as follows. Initially reduce every positive component power by a factor $1-\varepsilon$, with $0<\varepsilon<1$. For user $i$ let $B_{i,j}$ be its input energy at coordinate $j$, averaged over the finitely many independent message indices of that user's codebook, including the cross term in $|U_i+V_i|^2$. Across coordinates the $B_{i,j}$ are IID; Jensen gives $\mathbb E B_{i,j}^2\le\mathbb E|U_i+V_i|^4=2((1-\varepsilon)P_i)^2$, independently of message-set size. Thus $\operatorname{Var}(n^{-1}\sum_j B_{i,j})\le2P_i^2/n$ and its mean is $(1-\varepsilon)P_i$. Chebyshev makes the probability of either power exceeding $P_i$ tend to zero. The ensemble average sum of receiver errors tends to zero by step 1.1; Markov makes the probability of an error larger than the square root of that average tend to zero. Hence some deterministic codebook simultaneously meets both exact average power constraints and has vanishing errors. If a user's total power is zero, its codeword is zero and its rate is zero. Fix $\varepsilon$ first, take the coding limit, and then let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$; continuity and closure give the claimed nonslack region. This argument also applies to every simpler Gaussian codebook used below.

The eight inequalities in step 1.1, with closure removing strictness, project exactly to the seven stated facets plus $r_1\le A_1+E_2$ and $r_2\le A_2+E_1$. Here is an explicit elimination. Set $S=r_1+r_2$, $l_1=\max(0,S-G_2)$, $l_2=\max(0,S-G_1)$, $v_1=\min(A_1,r_1)$, $v_2=\min(A_2,r_2)$. The private rates must lie in $[l_i,v_i]$ and satisfy $r_1-E_2\le p_1-p_2\le E_1-r_2$. Such rates exist exactly when $l_i\le v_i$ and the intervals $[l_1-v_2,v_1-l_2]$ and $[r_1-E_2,E_1-r_2]$ intersect. Expanding the max/min comparisons gives $S\le A_1+G_2$, $S\le A_2+G_1$, $r_1\le A_1+E_2$, $r_2\le A_2+E_1$, $S\le E_1+E_2$, $2r_1+r_2\le A_1+G_1+E_2$, $r_1+2r_2\le A_2+G_2+E_1$, together with $r_i\le D_i$. The other comparisons are redundant: $r_i\le G_i$ follows from $D_i\le G_i$, and $S\le G_2+E_1$ or $S\le G_1+E_2$ follows from $S\le E_1+E_2$ and $E_i\le G_i$; the remaining inequalities are nonnegativity of the Gaussian mutual informations. Conversely these same comparisons ensure the intervals intersect, providing the desired $p_i$.

Suppose $r_1>A_1+E_2$. The seven facets give $r_2<G_2-E_2$ from $S\le A_1+G_2$, $r_2<E_1-A_1$ from $S\le E_1+E_2$, $S<G_1$ from $2r_1+r_2\le A_1+G_1+E_2$, and $r_1\le D_1$. Use a single Gaussian user 1 codebook of full power $P_1$ and only the nominal common user 2 power $P_{2c}$, carrying all of user 2's information; set its private layer to zero. At receiver 1 the MAC own-message bound is at least $D_1$, its user 2 bound is at least $E_1-A_1=I(U_2;Y_1|U_1)$, and its sum bound is at least $G_1$: removing the independent private user 2 signal only reduces noise, and conditioning additionally on the entire $X_1$ increases the user 2 bound. Receiver 2's Gaussian treating-user-1-as-noise bound is at least $G_2-E_2=I(U_2;Y_2)$ computed under the nominal law, because the private user 2 satellite has been removed. These four inequalities are precisely the Gaussian two-codeword MAC tests at receiver 1 and the single-codeword test at receiver 2; the likelihood-ratio union proof in step 1.1 with two streams proves achievability directly. The sum of the powers used is no larger than the prescribed powers, and step 2.1 selects deterministic power-feasible codebooks. This describes the changed labels and powers explicitly: all user 1 information is private at the unintended receiver, so its actual private INR can exceed the nominal $q_1$; user 2 uses only its nominal common power.

If instead $r_2>A_2+E_1$, reflect the construction in step 4.1. Both extra individual inequalities cannot fail together, since that would give $S>A_1+A_2+E_1+E_2\ge E_1+E_2$, contradicting a stated sum facet. When neither fails use step 3.1. Equality cases follow by closure of these achievable regions and the power-slack limit in step 2.1. If a layer is singleton it contributes no competing index; if both rates are zero use the all-zero code. This proves the entire seven-facet region, with the explicit nominal-policy and auxiliary-removal convention in the statement.
